the barrier height of Na/GaAs(110), like other metal/GaAs(100) interfaces, is determined primarily by the Fermi level pinning at the interface.

Na forms a Schottky barrier on n-type GaAs with an unusually low barrier height of about 0·7 V, despite its low work function and electronegativity, and that the Fermi level is pinned at about 2·2 eV above the GaAs valence-band maximum.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, despite the fact that the Na work function is much smaller than that of GaAs and that the electronegativity difference between GaAs and Na is also small, the Schottky barrier formed by Na on the cleaved GaAs surface is not significantly different from that formed by other metals.

the Schottky barrier heights of Na/n-GaAS(110) diodes, as well as the metal-induced semiconductor band bending measured in photoemission, are consistent with the metal-semiconductor interface being a simple metal-semiconductor contact rather than a dipole layer.

, for a metal-semiconductor system with such a large metal-induced gap state density, it is possible to extract the Schottky barrier using a simple model, provided the metal-induced gap state band is not strongly coupled to the semiconductor valence band.
